title: Regular -er Verbs
subtitle: parler: je parle, tu parles, il parle, nous parlons, vous parlez, ils parlent. The most common verb pattern in French.
objectives: Conjugate any regular -er verb in the present indicative.
Recognize the six persons: je, tu, il/elle, nous, vous, ils/elles.
Understand that the -e, -es, -e, -ent endings are silent.

sections.heading: The -er verbs
sections.body:
The largest class of French verbs end in -er in the infinitive. These verbs follow a regular pattern in the present tense.

Infinitive: parler (to speak)

Present indicative:
  je parle       (I speak)
  tu parles      (you speak, familiar)
  il/elle parle  (he/she speaks)
  nous parlons   (we speak)
  vous parlez    (you speak, formal/plural)
  ils/elles parlent (they speak)

The endings -e, -es, -e, and -ent are all silent. Only the nous and vous forms have audible endings: -ons, -ez.

sections.heading: The paradigm table
sections.body:
parler (to speak)

  je         parl-e      [paʁl]
  tu         parl-es     [paʁl]
  il/elle    parl-e      [paʁl]
  nous       parl-ons    [paʁlɔ̃]
  vous       parl-ez     [paʁle]
  ils/elles  parl-ent    [paʁl]

Notice that je, tu, il, and ils all sound the same: [paʁl]. The distinction is made by the subject pronoun, not the verb form.

sections.heading: Other common -er verbs
sections.body:
aimer (to love, to like)
  j'aime, tu aimes, il aime, nous aimons, vous aimez, ils aiment

donner (to give)
  je donne, tu donnes, il donne, nous donnons, vous donnez, ils donnent

chanter (to sing)
  je chante, tu chantes, il chante, nous chantons, vous chantez, ils chantent

All follow the same pattern. Learn one, and you know thousands.

sections.heading: Practice from Molière
sections.body:
From Le Misanthrope:

  Je veux qu'on soit sincère.
  (I want one to be sincere.)

Here 'veux' is irregular (from vouloir), but the pattern extends: sincere speech is what the speaker wants.

sections.heading: Verbs to practice
sections.instructions: Conjugate each verb aloud in all six persons.
